chapter_title: Chương 24: 0024【Chúng Tôi Mở Server Lậu, Không Bán Đồ】

segments.title: Chương 24: 0024【Chúng Tôi Mở Server Lậu, Không Bán Đồ】
segments.content:
Tao Chenggang stopped drinking liquor and took a sip of tea instead, letting himself sober up a little. "What other business is there to talk about?"

"A *Legend* private server," Chen Guiliang said.

Tao Chenggang couldn't help but laugh. "Private servers are a tough business these days; there's just too much competition. I can't even be bothered to pull people from online anymore. I just run the servers for internet cafes on the side. The private servers for the eight internet cafes I manage, after giving the admins their cut of the recharges, only earn me a few hundred to a thousand yuan a month. It's just pocket money."

Chen Guiliang said, "We could do a different kind of private server."

Thinking back on Chen Guiliang's previous ingenious ideas, Tao Chenggang didn't immediately refuse. Instead, he said, "Tell me more, little brother."

Chen Guiliang said:

"Why are private servers so hard to make money with now? It's simply a matter of technology."

"The technology is in the hands of a few studios and experts. What they release for free or for cheap is basically outdated tech. This has led to the current state of *Legend* private servers: numerous, yet severely homogenized, holding no appeal for players."

"If you want to be appealing, you have to spend money to buy their modification tools, or buy their private server frameworks directly. They sell their technology at high prices to make money, while developing more new features to slowly phase out the old private server versions."

"Some people even enter the scene themselves with their technology, creating the hottest and most profitable private servers. And you guys simply can't compete. Isn't that right?"

Tao Chenggang agreed, "That's about the situation. You have the technology?"

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "I don't understand the technology, but I understand the market."

"You mean that different kind of private server you mentioned?" Tao Chenggang asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Before level 40, you level up after killing just a few mobs. After level 40, the leveling speed is still much faster than the official server. The drop rates for equipment like the Dragon Tooth and Raging Cleaver can also be set super high. Even if players don't recharge, they can still get all Six Major Armors. Equipment that costs money on other private servers can be obtained for free on ours."

Yang Yuhui couldn't help but interject, "If we let people get those top-tier items for free, how are we supposed to make money selling equipment later?"

"Our private server doesn't sell equipment! That's our core selling point," Chen Guiliang said with a mysterious smile.

Yang Yuhui said, "If we don't sell equipment, how can a private server make money? We're not running a charity."

But Tao Chenggang's mind was sparked. "Use that free-to-play monetization method?"

Yang Yuhui was skeptical. "Those monetization methods require adding too many features. I'm one hundred percent certain that no private server operator in all of China could develop them within one or two years."

Chen Guiliang smiled without saying a word.

His curiosity thoroughly piqued, Tao Chenggang quickly poured Chen Guiliang a drink. "Little brother, stop keeping us in suspense."

"Dungeons," Chen Guiliang said.

Yang Yuhui asked, "What's a dungeon?"

*Endless Quest* already had dungeons, but they didn't get much attention.

Chen Guiliang said, "An independent game map, it doesn't need to be very large. Players need a specific method to enter the dungeon to fight monsters. Only after players team up will they enter the same dungeon, so there's no need to worry about others stealing your kills."

Tao Chenggang smiled. "That's an interesting way to play."

"The top-tier equipment that other private servers sell for money, our players can get on the regular maps," Chen Guiliang said. "But by entering dungeon maps, they can get overpowered equipment. We don't sell that overpowered equipment. We only sell tickets to enter the dungeons."

"That's a great idea!"

Yang Yuhui clapped his hands in approval. "Why do current private servers stop being profitable after just a few days? Because they're too boring. Before recharging, players can't beat those who pay for equipment, so over time, they get bored. And after paying for equipment, they get too lazy to fight mobs and just PK all day. Mindlessly PK-ing back and forth gets boring too."

"In other words, after playing on a private server for a few days, players don't know what to do anymore."

"The idea of selling dungeon tickets is great. Paying players don't buy equipment directly; they still have to grind for it themselves. At the same time, paying creates a gap between them and the free players, satisfying their vanity."

Tao Chenggang voiced a concern, "If there's a secret map that free players can't enter, and they can't even touch the overpowered equipment, we won't be able to retain free players either. Eventually, that will lead to a loss of paying players."

Chen Guiliang said, "Then, on the top-tier regular maps, we can have an extremely low drop rate for overpowered equipment. But don't let everything overpowered drop. Accessories can drop, to give free players some hope. But for overpowered weapons and armor, they should forever remain in the realm of legends that 'might drop'. This gives ordinary players a glimmer of hope, yet makes it forever unattainable."

"Haha, you're too devious!" Yang Yuhui laughed.

Tao Chenggang asked, "What's the most suitable price for a dungeon ticket? If it's too low, it'll be hard for us to make money. If it's too high, it'll scare away a lot of players."

"Give me a pen and paper," Chen Guiliang said.

Tao Chenggang quickly handed them over.

Chen Guiliang scribbled on the paper as he spoke:

"First, a low-price strategy to attract more players to pay and participate. For example, 10 yuan for one ticket, 100 yuan for twelve. Encourage players to repeatedly enter dungeons to grind. Encourage a whale to gift tickets to his underlings, leading a whole group into the dungeons."

"Second, the dungeon BOSS can't be something a player can solo. If it's too easy to kill, paying players will get bored after running the dungeon a few times. At the same time, this forces more people to buy tickets and team up to enter. But not too many people, because there won't be enough overpowered equipment to go around. It's best if a dungeon BOSS can be taken down by 3 to 5 people."

"Third, design dungeons of varying difficulties, with different drop rates and ticket prices for each. For instance, a dungeon with 5-yuan tickets can be for players who have just started recharging. Because their equipment isn't that good yet, they can't handle bosses that are too difficult."

"Fourth, each dungeon run is guaranteed to drop at least one piece of overpowered equipment, and occasionally it can drop an extra one or two. However, these guaranteed overpowered drops should all be mainly accessories. To get weapons and armor, they must repeatedly spend money to run the dungeons."

"As for those guaranteed overpowered items, after paying players run the maps multiple times, they'll definitely have extras they don't need. They can then gift them to ordinary players. It's like making friends or recruiting underlings. This will boost the morale of ordinary players and also satisfy the vanity of paying players."

Tao Chenggang suggested, "We can port those overpowered items from *Legend of Mir 3* and just change their names."

"No!"

Yang Yuhui objected again. "Equipment ported from *Legend of Mir 3* to private servers often bugs out and doesn't display correctly. A player might have paid for equipment, but they look like they're not wearing any clothes and have no weapon in hand. When they PK, they're basically naked, punching people, doing high damage but looking ridiculous."

Chen Guiliang said, "Then let's use the original *Legend* weapons and change their stats and names. For example, the Raging Cleaver, we'll change the overpowered version to 'Heaven-Cleaving Raging Cleaver.' The Dragon Tooth to 'Heaven-Suppressing Dragon Tooth,' and the Unfettered Fan to 'Mystic-Sky Unfettered Fan.' The Heaven-Demon Armor to 'Abyssal Heaven-Demon Armor.' By the way, is it possible to cosmetically enhance parts of the equipment without causing bugs?"

"Yes, it is." Yang Yuhui also knew a bit about the technical side.

Chen Guiliang asked again, "There are no technical issues with making dungeons, right?"

"No problem," Yang Yuhui said. "Tools like map duplicators and map converters can all be bought from experts. I can even modify them myself. But if I do it, there might be bugs that need repeated adjustments."

Chen Guiliang continued, "After the private server goes live, get a group of studio employees to play."

Tao Chenggang smiled. "Shills!"

Not bad, Boss Tao.

Look at him, he's learned to answer before I do.

Yang Yuhui asked, "What are shills?"

Tao Chenggang explained it in detail.

"Damn," Yang Yuhui exclaimed after hearing the explanation. "Using shills like this is a damn good way to trick those rich people. Give this task to me. I'll personally play a female character and wrap them around my little finger."

Chen Guiliang asked, "About how much would it cost to make a private server with this kind of framework?"

Tao Chenggang estimated, "If we only add the currently mature features, without adding any other new functions, and just copy maps to create dungeons, it should be possible for three to five thousand yuan. To prevent too many bugs, I'll find a reliable expert, and at most, it would be around ten thousand. Promoting on major forums to attract people also costs money, and renting a decent server costs money too. The initial investment would be around twenty to thirty thousand, maybe even thirty to forty thousand."

"How do players recharge nowadays?" Chen Guiliang knew, but he was afraid of getting something wrong.

Tao Chenggang said:

"For a legitimate game, they rely on distributors selling point cards. For example, Shanda initially entrusted Ubisoft with selling their point cards, and they had to pay Ubisoft a 33% commission. Plus, Ubisoft often delayed payments."

"In a fit of anger, Shanda created its own sales channel, developing a 'Cafe e-Sale System.' Internet cafes that sold Shanda point cards could get a commission of 8% to 10%."

"So Shanda is very formidable. As long as their games aren't too bad, they can pull them up through their sales channels. Because 70% of the internet cafes in the country have already formed a community of shared interests with Shanda. And it's also very convenient for players; they can just go to an internet cafe and ask the admin to recharge for them."

Chen Guiliang asked again, "What about private servers?"

"Bank transfers, postal remittances," Tao Chenggang said.

Chen Guiliang sighed internally: What a fucking primitive and crude way to recharge!

But for now, there was no way around the current situation.

Even when buying things on Taobao at this time, you first paid Alipay, and only after Alipay received the money would they notify the seller to ship the goods.

Strictly speaking, what Alipay was doing was illegal. It would still be another year before they could clear the hurdles with the banks.

And when Qidian Chinese Network paid royalties to its authors, the site's owner would ride a motorcycle to the post office to remit the money. There was one impressive author who would demand his royalties as soon as he had accumulated fifty yuan. The site owner was driven so crazy that he raised the minimum payout amount to 200 yuan.

I just watched an interview with Wandering Toad yesterday. He said Qidian also had a tough time in the beginning. If it weren't for him, it might have gone under.

The online banking services of the Big Four banks had been successively launched two or three years ago, but very few people used them.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What about recharging via mobile phone SMS?"

Tao Chenggang said, "That requires a partnership with China Mobile, which is a bit difficult to arrange. Moreover, China Mobile usually takes a 50% cut, which is even more ruthless than the traditional distributors' 33%."

Yang Yuhui said, "Actually, collecting money is pretty easy. Players who want to buy dungeon tickets can contact us through QQ. If they want to buy ten tickets at once, the player sends me their game ID, and after I receive the bank transfer, I'll grant them access to the dungeon ten times."

How complicated. Many players who might have wanted to recharge on impulse would give up because of these procedures.

Nothing to be done. The times were a constraint.

"Let's talk about the investment and profit sharing for the private server." Chen Guiliang finally bared his fangs.
